name: Open Slots Finder
idea: A filterable directory of artists and makers who currently have commission slots open, with price range, style and queue status.
description: Buyers of art, emotes, VTuber assets, game art and custom costumes currently hunt through social posts to find someone who is taking orders. This directory lets makers keep a profile (links to their own portfolio and own payment page, no money handled here) with a live open/closed/waitlist status, price bands and style tags, and lets buyers filter by type, budget and availability. Start with one tight vertical (for example Twitch/VTuber assets, or fursuit makers) so the list is complete and trusted before widening.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel hobby, Supabase Postgres + magic-link auth for makers to update their own status; profiles hold links and tiny thumbnails only, no image hosting.
why_hard_to_copy: The code is easy; the moat is a hand-seeded, vetted maker list in one vertical and makers who keep their open/closed status fresh (network effect in a small niche). A clone with an empty directory is useless.

signals.summary: Wants a site to browse artists who have commissions open and search them by art type and price.
Wishes there were a Skeb-style commission site for artists outside Japan.
Asks where a non-artist friend can find an artist for Twitch emotes that is not Fiverr or Etsy.
Looking for where to find a capsule artist for a Steam game and asks whether a site specialising in this exists; says if not, there should be one.
Says fursuit makers are hard to find and wishes one website listed every maker so they could filter by price and type.

competitors_seen.name: Artists&Clients
competitors_seen.note: Commissions marketplace with filtering; listing is thin, not verified live.

competitors_seen.name: ArtStation / Behance
competitors_seen.note: Portfolio platforms; not built around an open-slots status.

competitors_seen.name: Individual maker Carrd pages (queue/slot status per maker)
competitors_seen.note: Web search found no fursuit maker directory with price filter or waitlist status; each maker publishes their own page.

satellite.name: Commission price and quote sheet generator
satellite.what: Free page where an artist fills in styles, prices and terms and gets a shareable price sheet / quote template.
satellite.why_shared: Every artist needs one and posts it in their bio, which exposes the directory link.
satellite.handoff: One button on the generated sheet: 'Show my open slots in the directory'.

marketing.target: Small digital artists and custom makers who want free visibility, and the buyers looking for them.
marketing.funnel: Maker sees the shared price sheet or a friend's profile, claims a free listing in two minutes, buyers find them by filter.
marketing.cold_outreach: DM 50 makers in one vertical offering to pre-fill their listing from their public pages, asking only for a yes.
post_ideas: Which emote artists have slots open this week (live list)
Free price sheet generator for commission artists
Price ranges for Twitch emote commissions, from listed profiles

capital_note: Domain only; Supabase free and Vercel hobby cover 500 monthly users.
notes: Five independent X posts over six months, all asking the same thing in different verticals (I merged the fursuit maker request in as a first vertical). Honest weakness: marketplace cold start and existing generic platforms. No payments are held, only links out. The fursuit request is a single post.

name: Mistria Farm Planner
idea: A tile-accurate drag-and-drop farm layout planner for Fields of Mistria, shareable by link.
description: Players of the farming sim Fields of Mistria want to plan their farm layout before placing and decorating in game, as Stardew players can. The planner would hold hand-measured footprints for buildings, crops, paths and decor, and the fixed anchors (farmhouse, shrine), with undo, layers and a share link. Hard to copy because the footprint and rule data must be measured and verified in game.
web_delivery: Static React/canvas app on Vercel; layouts saved as compressed JSON in the URL, optional Supabase table for named saves.
why_hard_to_copy: Needs a hand-verified dataset of tile footprints and placement rules for each object, plus patch tracking; generic grid editors do not have it.

signals.summary: Asks whether a website exists to plan a Mistria farm before decorating in game, notes one exists for Stardew, and says planning on a large scale in her head is hard.

competitors_seen.name: fieldsofmistria.it.com farm layout guide
competitors_seen.note: Unofficial text guide, not an interactive planner.

competitors_seen.name: Fields of Mistria wiki (wiki.gg)
competitors_seen.note: Wiki; I could not confirm it has an interactive layout planner.

satellite.name: Mistria object size cheat sheet
satellite.what: Searchable table of every placeable object and its tile footprint.
satellite.why_shared: Players link it in guides and Discords.
satellite.handoff: Each row has an 'add to planner' button.

where: Fields of Mistria Discord and community forums
marketing.target: Fields of Mistria players who plan layouts and decorate.
marketing.funnel: Cheat sheet in search results, then the planner, then the share link posted in Discord.
marketing.cold_outreach: Message popular layout-sharing players asking to import their screenshots as template layouts.
post_ideas: Plan your Mistria farm before year 1 (free tile planner)
Every Mistria object by tile size
Template layouts from the community

notes: One post. A grid editor is a weekend job; the defensible part is the verified footprint data and keeping up with patches. Game-specific audience size is unknown.

name: Hours Any Day
idea: A web reader for the Liturgy of the Hours that opens any past or future date with the correct calendar rules.
description: A user who missed two days through illness could not open them in the app she uses, which only goes back one day. A web app would compute the liturgical day correctly (season, feast precedence, psalter week, local calendar) and show the prayers for any date, installable as a PWA with offline caching. Correct calendar logic is the hard part.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel hobby; calendar rules computed client-side; texts stored as static JSON or in Supabase.
why_hard_to_copy: Liturgical calendar precedence rules (Easter computation, solemnities vs memorials, national and diocesan proper calendars) are correctness-critical and rarely implemented well; offline PWA.

signals.summary: Missed two days due to illness and asks for a website that shows Liturgy of the Hours for past days, because the iBreviary app only goes back one day.

competitors_seen.name: Universalis
competitors_seen.note: Paid app that views any date, past, present or future.

competitors_seen.name: DivineOffice.org (per forum thread)
competitors_seen.note: Popular choice, but a poster said access had become restricted.

satellite.name: Liturgical calendar date lookup
satellite.what: Enter any date and see the season, feast rank and color for the chosen calendar.
satellite.why_shared: Parish staff and bloggers link to it for date questions.
satellite.handoff: Link button 'Open the prayers for this day'.

where: Parish staff and music director forums (for example musicasacra.com)
marketing.target: Laypeople and clergy who pray the Hours and want free access to any date.
marketing.funnel: Calendar lookup search traffic, then the reader.
marketing.cold_outreach: Offer the calendar lookup to parish-tech newsletters.
post_ideas: Missed a few days? Open any date of the Hours
Why the calendar differs by country, explained with the rules

notes: One post. New niche 'Faith & Religion' because no canonical niche fits. Big risk: the official English breviary texts are copyrighted, so a launch needs public-domain or openly licensed texts or a licence; check this first.

name: Disc Edition Database
idea: A community database of physical film releases (editions, barcodes, special features), like Discogs but for movies.
description: A collector wants a Discogs-style site to see every physical release of a film. The site would hold one page per edition with barcode, region, cuts, extras and packaging, and let users add copies to a collection or wantlist. Barcode scanning runs in the browser camera.
web_delivery: Next.js + Supabase; barcode lookup in browser with a JS decoder; no image hosting beyond small cover thumbnails.
why_hard_to_copy: The edition database itself: community-curated, cross-linked by barcode, with a moderation process; code is not the moat.

signals.summary: Wishes for a Discogs-like website for films to see all physical releases.

competitors_seen.name: Movie Collector Shelf
competitors_seen.note: iOS personal collection manager with a community catalog; not a public edition database.

satellite.name: Edition comparison page
satellite.what: Enter a film and compare known releases side by side (cut, region, extras).

where: Physical media collector forums and Discords
marketing.funnel: Edition comparison pages in search, then free accounts to track a collection.
marketing.cold_outreach: Ask forum collectors to seed one label's releases.
post_ideas: Every edition of one cult film compared
Which boutique labels have the most complete cuts

notes: One post. I did not verify other existing physical-media databases (such as Blu-ray.com); the scorer should check how well they cover this before rating.

name: Duo Pose Studio
idea: A browser posing mannequin for multiple figures that interact (hug, fight, hold hands), shareable by link.
description: Artists want pose-reference sites that work for more than one person in frame and are not just a Pinterest board. A 3D mannequin tool with a library of hand-authored two-figure interaction poses, contact constraints and camera angles, running client side, fills that. The ability to save a scene as a link avoids storing images.
web_delivery: Three.js app on Vercel; poses as small JSON; scenes saved in the URL or a Supabase row.
why_hard_to_copy: Needs a hand-authored library of believable two-figure poses with contact constraints (inverse kinematics), which takes art and rigging skill.

signals.summary: Wants a website like Line of Action but with several people in the frame interacting.
Asks for a pose gallery website that is not Pinterest, and whether Line of Action has a gallery mode.

name: Scene Soundtrack Lookup

why_hard_to_copy: A curated, moderated, timestamped dataset with contributors is the moat; cold start is brutal.

name: Play It Online Board Games
idea: A directory of which board games can be played online with friends, on which platform, free or paid, and how good the implementation is.
description: A user asks whether anyone has built a repository of all board games playable online with friends. The directory would map each game to its online implementations, price, player counts, supports voice and async play, and user ratings of the implementation quality. It links out to the platforms, no game engine hosted.
web_delivery: Next.js + Supabase; filterable table with user-submitted implementation records; no real-time play hosted.
why_hard_to_copy: The cross-platform dataset (which game is on which of the dozen platforms and how it plays) is hand-curated and goes stale, so ongoing curation is the moat.

name: If Something Happens Binder
idea: A private, client-side encrypted 'what to do if I die or am ill' binder for family, with a guided checklist and trusted-contact release.
description: A user wants a site or app to help prepare a book of instructions for her children covering her and her husband's affairs. The app would give a guided checklist of what to record (accounts, contacts, wishes, locations of documents), encrypt everything in the browser, and release it to named contacts after a missed check-in. It is a notes organiser, not legal advice or a will service, and holds no money.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; WebCrypto encryption in the browser; Supabase stores only ciphertext; pg_cron check-in emails via a free email tier.
why_hard_to_copy: Client-side encryption with a trustworthy recovery and release design plus expert-written, country-specific checklists; mistakes here are costly.

signals.summary: Wishes for a website or app that helps prepare a book of instructions for her children so her and her husband's affairs are sorted if something happens.

competitors_seen.name: Everplans
competitors_seen.note: Paid, around $75 to $100 a year per one blog.

competitors_seen.name: Digital Legacy Vault and others
competitors_seen.note: Newer vault apps with delayed release; SecureSafe and Life Safe Legacy have paid tiers.

satellite.name: First 48 hours checklist
satellite.what: Printable checklist for a family after a death or hospitalisation, by country.
satellite.why_shared: Widely shared in family and support groups.
satellite.handoff: Button to build your own binder.

marketing.target: Adults 45 to 70 organising for their children.
marketing.cold_outreach: Offer the checklist to caregiver newsletters.
post_ideas: What your kids will need to know if you are unreachable
The one-page checklist for the first 48 hours

notes: One post, though crowded competitor set shows the need is real. Liability and security burden are high for a solo developer; keep it a document organiser, with no passwords by default, and no legal advice (legal services are banned in the spec).

name: ALPR Incident Ledger
idea: A sourced ledger of documented license-plate-reader misuse cases and documented solved cases by city.
description: People on opposite sides of the debate want an aggregation of documented Flock camera incidents: one wants misuse by police compiled, another wants a list of crimes the cameras deterred or solved. A ledger with citations, dates and public-records links per city would serve both, separated from the camera location maps that already exist.
web_delivery: Next.js + Supabase table of incidents with source URLs; editor workflow for submissions; static pages per city.
why_hard_to_copy: Editorial rigor: each entry needs a primary source and consistent classification, which takes sustained curation; local public-records requests make it better over time.

signals.summary: Asks whether a website compiles abuses of Flock cameras by police, citing cases in several states.
Asks for a website listing crimes Flock cameras have deterred and criminals they helped catch.

competitors_seen.note: Volunteer map of ALPR locations, not an incident ledger.

competitors_seen.name: Local news how-to guides on finding Flock cameras
competitors_seen.note: Search tools such as Have I Been Flocked and Eyes On Flock are mentioned by search results; I did not open them.

where: Civil liberties groups and local government watchdog communities
marketing.target: Residents, journalists and council staff researching ALPR contracts.
marketing.funnel: City pages in search, then submissions.
marketing.cold_outreach: Offer the ledger to reporters covering a local contract vote.
post_ideas: Every documented misuse case in one state with sources
What the city audit logs actually showed

name: Doctor Supply Atlas

description: One user asks for a website tracking the number of licensed physicians by state and which medical schools they graduated from. The app would merge public state medical board statistics into one comparable dataset with charts and downloads. State formats differ, so the data work is the product.

why_hard_to_copy: Requires normalising fragmented public board data across states into a consistent schema, updated periodically; a one-off scraper does not stay current.

name: Crossover Issue Finder
idea: Pick two comic characters and see every issue they both appear in.
description: A reader wants a site like a DC character guide that lists all appearances of a character and also lists the comics two characters share. This is a join over a character-appearance dataset, with fuzzy name merging and reading-order links.
web_delivery: Next.js + Supabase Postgres with a pre-built appearance table; queries run server side.
why_hard_to_copy: Cleaning and merging character-appearance data from open sources (aliases, versions, teams) is the work; the query itself is trivial.

name: Pull Log
idea: A pull and collection logger for card and gacha games with per-account hit-rate stats.
description: Fans of rhythm and card games want a place to log which cards and costumes they own, as an older tracker did for another franchise, and card pack openers want to track packs opened per account with hit percentages to see who is lucky. One logger per game with a curated card list and optional shared community pull-rate statistics would serve both.
web_delivery: Next.js + Supabase; per-game card datasets as static JSON; users log pulls manually or via CSV paste.
why_hard_to_copy: Per-game curated card/costume data and crowd-sourced pull statistics only matter at volume; each game needs maintenance.

name: Fan Gallery Hub
idea: A link-based gallery of fan art and fan merch for one creator's community, with credits to the original artists.
description: A VTuber with commissioned and gifted art wants a gallery showing the pieces with credit to each artist, and a fan wants an online artist alley compiling all fan-made merch for a talent group. A hub that stores links, credits and tags (not image files) lets communities browse by artist, character and merch type.
web_delivery: Next.js + Supabase table of entries (external URL, artist handle, tags); previews through official embeds or thumbnails; no image storage.
why_hard_to_copy: Community curation and permissions (artist opt-in, takedown handling) in one fandom; weak technical moat.
